title.en: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change

chapterTag.category: AP Calc AB Unit 6 — Integration & Accumulation

body.en: Unit 6 unites differential and integral calculus through the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. We construct the definite integral from the ground up as a limit of Riemann sums, establish rigorous overestimate/underestimate criteria based on monotonicity and concavity, differentiate accumulation functions via the Leibniz rule, and master analytical integration techniques including u-substitution and inverse trigonometric forms.
body.ar: Unit 6 unites differential and التكامل التفاضل والتكامل through the Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل. We construct the definite التكامل from the ground up as a النهاية of Riemann sums, establish rigorous overestimate/underestimate criteria based on monotonicity and concavity, differentiate accumulation الدوال via the Leibniz rule, and master analytical integration techniques including u-substitution and inverse trigonometric forms.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Riemann Sums & Definite Integral Definition

body.en: The definite integral is defined rigorously as the limit of Riemann sums as the partition norm approaches zero. The relationship between the approximating rectangles and the true area depends directly on the function's monotonicity and concavity.
body.ar: The definite التكامل is defined rigorously as the النهاية of Riemann sums as the partition norm approaches zero. The relationship between the approximating rectangles and the true المساحة depends directly on the الدالة's monotonicity and concavity.

label.en: ● The Definite Integral as a Limit of Riemann Sums
label.ar: ● The Definite التكامل as a النهاية of Riemann Sums

body.en:
Let \(f\) be continuous on \([a, b]\). Partition \([a, b]\) into \(n\) subintervals of equal width \(\Delta x = \frac{b - a}{n}\), with grid points \(x_i = a + i\Delta x\). The definite integral of \(f\) from \(a\) to \(b\) is defined as: \[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)\,\Delta x \] where \(x_i^* \in [x_{i-1}, x_i]\) is an arbitrary sample point within the \(i\)-th subinterval.

Standard choices of sample points generate classical numerical approximations:

  • Left Riemann Sum: \(x_i^* = x_{i-1} \implies L_n = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} f(x_i)\,\Delta x\)
  • Right Riemann Sum: \(x_i^* = x_i \implies R_n = \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i)\,\Delta x\)
  • Midpoint Riemann Sum: \(x_i^* = \frac{x_{i-1} + x_i}{2} \implies M_n = \sum_{i=1}^n f\left(\frac{x_{i-1}+x_i}{2}\right)\,\Delta x\)
  • Trapezoidal Rule: \(T_n = \frac{L_n + R_n}{2} = \frac{\Delta x}{2}\left[ f(x_0) + 2f(x_1) + 2f(x_2) + \cdot s + 2f(x_{n-1}) + f(x_n) \right]\)

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change)

body.en:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts formula:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product derivative: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).
body.ar:
Why Integration by Parts & Integrating Factors Work: Differentiating a product \(u(x)v(x)\) gives \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\). Integrating both sides and rearranging yields the Integration by Parts الصيغة:

\[ \int u\,\frac{dv}{dx}\,dx = u v - \int v\,\frac{du}{dx}\,dx \]

Similarly, for a linear first-order ODE \(y' + P(x)y = Q(x)\), multiplying by the integrating factor \(\mu(x) = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\) (which satisfies \(\mu'(x) = P(x)\mu(x)\)) collapses the left-hand side into an exact product المشتقة: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[\mu(x)y\bigr] = \mu(x)Q(x)\).

body.en:
Part A: Water flows out of a reservoir at rate \(R(t)\) gal/hr given by the table below. Use a Trapezoidal Sum with the 3 subintervals indicated to approximate \(\int_0^{10} R(t)\,dt\). If \(R''(t) > 0\), is your approximation an overestimate or underestimate?

\(t\) (hours)03710
\(R(t)\) (gal/hr)120906550

Part B: Express the limit as a definite integral and evaluate: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \left( 1 + \frac{3i}{n} \right)^2 \frac{3}{n} \]

Solution:

Part A: Notice subintervals have unequal widths: \(\Delta t_1 = 3 - 0 = 3\), \(\Delta t_2 = 7 - 3 = 4\), \(\Delta t_3 = 10 - 7 = 3\). Calculate trapezoidal areas individually: \[ T_1 = \frac{3}{2}(120 + 90) = \frac{3}{2}(210) = 315 \] \[ T_2 = \frac{4}{2}(90 + 65) = 2(155) = 310 \] \[ T_3 = \frac{3}{2}(65 + 50) = \frac{3}{2}(115) = 172.5 \] \[ \int_0^{10} R(t)\,dt \approx 315 + 310 + 172.5 = \mathbf{797.5\text{ gallons}}. \] Since \(R''(t) > 0\), the rate function is strictly concave up on \([0, 10]\). The secant line chords lie above the curve on each subinterval, so \(797.5\text{ gal}\) is an overestimate.

Part B: Match with \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(a + i\Delta x)\Delta x\). Here \(\Delta x = \frac{3}{n} = \frac{b - a}{n}\). Choose \(a = 1\), so \(b - a = 3 \implies b = 4\). The sample points are \(x_i = 1 + \frac{3i}{n}\), and \(f(x) = x^2\). Thus: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(1 + \frac{3i}{n}\right)^2 \frac{3}{n} = \int_1^4 x^2\,dx = \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_1^4 = \frac{64}{3} - \frac{1}{3} = \mathbf{21}. \]

Solution:

Part A: Notice subintervals have unequal widths: \(\Delta t_1 = 3 - 0 = 3\), \(\Delta t_2 = 7 - 3 = 4\), \(\Delta t_3 = 10 - 7 = 3\). احسب trapezoidal areas individually: \[ T_1 = \frac{3}{2}(120 + 90) = \frac{3}{2}(210) = 315 \] \[ T_2 = \frac{4}{2}(90 + 65) = 2(155) = 310 \] \[ T_3 = \frac{3}{2}(65 + 50) = \frac{3}{2}(115) = 172.5 \] \[ \int_0^{10} R(t)\,dt \approx 315 + 310 + 172.5 = \mathbf{797.5\text{ gallons}}. \] Since \(R''(t) > 0\), the rate الدالة is strictly concave up on \([0, 10]\). The secant line chords lie above the curve on each subinterval, so \(797.5\text{ gal}\) is an overestimate.

Part B: Match with \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(a + i\Delta x)\Delta x\). Here \(\Delta x = \frac{3}{n} = \frac{b - a}{n}\). Choose \(a = 1\), so \(b - a = 3 \implies b = 4\). body.en:
Problem (Easy): Consider the function \( f(x) = 4 \). What is the value of the definite integral \( \int_{3}^{6} f(x) \, dx \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: The definite integral \( \int_{a}^{b} c \, dx \) where c is a constant represents the area of a rectangle with height c and width \( b-a \). In this case, \( c = 4 \), \( a = 3 \), and \( b = 6 \). Therefore, the value of the integral is \( 4 \times (6-3) = 4 \times 3 = 12 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): Consider the الدالة \( f(x) = 4 \). What is the value of the definite التكامل \( \int_{3}^{6} f(x) \, dx \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: The definite التكامل \( \int_{a}^{b} c \, dx \) حيث c is a الثابت represents the المساحة of a rectangle with height c and width \( b-a \). In this case, \( c = 4 \), \( a = 3 \), and \( b = 6 \). وبالتالي, the value of the التكامل is \( 4 \times (6-3) = 4 \times 3 = 12 \).

label.en: ⚠️ Common Exam Traps — Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change
label.ar: ⚠️ أخطاء شائعة في الاختبار — Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change

body.en:
1. Adding \(+C\) Only After Exponentiating in Separable ODEs: In \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4xy\), integrating gives \(\ln|y| = \tfrac{4}{2}x^2 + C \implies y = Ae^{4x^2/2}\) where \(A = \pm e^C\). Writing \(y = e^{4x^2/2} + C\) is a fatal algebraic error that forfeits all follow-up marks on College Board AP Calculus AB.

2. Forgetting to Transform Limits in \(u\)-Substitution: In definite integrals \(\int_a^b f(g(x))g'(x)\,dx\), you must replace the limits \(x = a, b\) with \(u = g(a), g(b)\) immediately.
body.ar:
1. Adding \(+C\) Only After Exponentiating in Separable ODEs: In \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4xy\), integrating gives \(\ln|y| = \tfrac{4}{2}x^2 + C \implies y = Ae^{4x^2/2}\) حيث \(A = \pm e^C\). Writing \(y = e^{4x^2/2} + C\) is a fatal algebraic error that forfeits all follow-up marks on College Board AP التفاضل والتكامل AB.

2. Forgetting to Transform النهايات in \(u\)-Substitution: In definite التكاملات \(\int_a^b f(g(x))g'(x)\,dx\), you must replace the النهايات \(x = a, b\) with \(u = g(a), g(b)\) immediately.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Express the following limit as a definite integral with lower limit \(a = 0\), and evaluate it: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{2}{n} \sqrt{4 - \left(\frac{2i}{n}\right)^2} \]
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

Express the following limit as a definite integral with lower limit \(a = 0\), and احسب قيمة it: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{2}{n} \sqrt{4 - \left(\frac{2i}{n}\right)^2} \]

solution.en: Identify components: \(\Delta x = \frac{2}{n}\), so with \(a = 0\), the upper limit is \(b = 2\). Sample points are \(x_i = \frac{2i}{n}\). The integrand is \(f(x) = \sqrt{4 - x^2}\). The limit becomes: \[ \int_0^2 \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx \] Geometrically, \(y = \sqrt{4 - x^2}\) represents the upper half of a circle of radius \(r = 2\) centered at the origin. The interval \([0, 2]\) represents one quarter of the circle: \[ \int_0^2 \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\pi r^2 = \frac{1}{4}\pi (2)^2 = \mathbf{\pi} \approx 3.1416. \]

label.en: ● Theorem & Proof: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC 1 & 2)
label.ar: ● مبرهنة & برهان: Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل (FTC 1 & 2)

body.en:
FTC Part 1 (Derivative of Accumulation): If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\), then the function \(g(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt\) is continuous on \([a, b]\), differentiable on \((a, b)\), and: \[ g'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\left[\int_a^x f(t)\,dt\right] = f(x) \]

Proof of FTC Part 1: By definition of the derivative: \[ g'(x) = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{g(x+h) - g(x)}{h} = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{1}{h}\left( \int_a^{x+h} f(t)\,dt - \int_a^x f(t)\,dt \right) = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{1}{h} \int_x^{x+h} f(t)\,dt \] By the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals, since \(f\) is continuous on \([x, x+h]\), there exists some \(c_h\) strictly between \(x\) and \(x+h\) such that: \[ \frac{1}{h}\int_x^{x+h} f(t)\,dt = f(c_h) \] Taking the limit as \(h \to 0\), the squeeze theorem forces \(c_h \to x\). Since \(f\) is continuous: \[ g'(x) = \lim_{h\to 0} f(c_h) = f(x). \quad \blacksquare \]

Leibniz Chain Rule Formula: For differentiable limit functions \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\): \[ \frac{d}{dx}\left[ \int_{u(x)}^{v(x)} f(t)\,dt \right] = f(v(x))\cdot v'(x) - f(u(x))\cdot u'(x) \]

FTC Part 2 (Evaluation Theorem): If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(F\) is any antiderivative of \(f\) (so \(F'(x) = f(x)\)), then: \[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a) = \left[ F(x) \right]_a^b \]
body.ar:
FTC Part 1 (المشتقة of Accumulation): If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\), then the الدالة \(g(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt\) is continuous on \([a, b]\), differentiable on \((a, b)\), and: \[ g'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\left[\int_a^x f(t)\,dt\right] = f(x) \]

Proof of FTC Part 1: By definition of the المشتقة: \[ g'(x) = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{g(x+h) - g(x)}{h} = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{1}{h}\left( \int_a^{x+h} f(t)\,dt - \int_a^x f(t)\,dt \right) = \lim_{h\to 0} \frac{1}{h} \int_x^{x+h} f(t)\,dt \] By the Mean Value مبرهنة for التكاملات, since \(f\) is continuous on \([x, x+h]\), there exists some \(c_h\) strictly between \(x\) and \(x+h\) such that: \[ \frac{1}{h}\int_x^{x+h} f(t)\,dt = f(c_h) \] Taking the النهاية as \(h \to 0\), the squeeze المبرهنة forces \(c_h \to x\). Since \(f\) is continuous: \[ g'(x) = \lim_{h\to 0} f(c_h) = f(x). \quad \blacksquare \]

Leibniz Chain Rule الصيغة: For differentiable النهاية الدوال \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\): \[ \frac{d}{dx}\left[ \int_{u(x)}^{v(x)} f(t)\,dt \right] = f(v(x))\cdot v'(x) - f(u(x))\cdot u'(x) \]

FTC Part 2 (Evaluation مبرهنة): If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(F\) is any antiderivative of \(f\) (so \(F'(x) = f(x)\)), then: \[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a) = \left[ F(x) \right]_a^b \]

label.en: Level 2 (Medium) — Worked Example · Piecewise Geometric Accumulation Function
label.ar: Level 2 (Medium) — مثال محلول · Piecewise Geometric Accumulation الدالة

body.en:
Problem: Let \(g(x) = \int_{-2}^x f(t)\,dt\) for \(-2 \le x \le 6\), where the continuous graph of \(f(t)\) consists of a semicircle of radius 2 from \(t = -2\) to \(t = 2\) located above the axis, followed by a line segment from \((2, 0)\) to \((6, -4)\).

  1. Evaluate \(g(2)\), \(g'(2)\), and \(g''(2)\) (or state DNE).
  2. Find all critical points of \(g\) on \((-2, 6)\) and classify them.
  3. Find the absolute maximum value of \(g\) on \([-2, 6]\).

Solution:

  1. \(g(2) = \int_{-2}^2 f(t)\,dt = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi(2)^2 = \mathbf{2\pi}\).
    By FTC Part 1: \(g'(x) = f(x) \implies g'(2) = f(2) = \mathbf{0}\).
    \(g''(x) = f'(x)\). The slope of the semicircle as \(t \to 2^-\) approaches \(-\infty\), while the line segment has slope \(m = \frac{-4 - 0}{6 - 2} = -1\). Thus \(g''(2) = f'(2)\) does not exist (corner/vertical tangent in \(f\)).
  2. Critical points of \(g\) occur when \(g'(x) = f(x) = 0\): on \((-2, 6)\), \(f(x) = 0\) at \(x = 2\). For \(x \in (-2, 2)\), \(f(x) > 0 \implies g'(x) > 0\). For \(x \in (2, 6)\), \(f(x) < 0 \implies g'(x) < 0\). Since \(g'\) changes from positive to negative at \(x = 2\), \(g\) has a relative maximum at \(x = 2\).
  3. Apply the Candidates Test on \([-2, 6]\):
    • Endpoint \(x = -2\): \(g(-2) = \int_{-2}^{-2} f(t)\,dt = 0\)
    • Critical point \(x = 2\): \(g(2) = 2\pi \approx 6.283\)
    • Endpoint \(x = 6\): \(g(6) = \int_{-2}^2 f(t)\,dt + \int_2^6 f(t)\,dt = 2\pi - \frac{1}{2}(4)(4) = 2\pi - 8 \approx -1.717\)
    The absolute maximum value of \(g\) is \(2\pi\), attained at \(x = 2\).

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Find the derivative \(h'(x)\) for the accumulation function: \[ h(x) = \int_{x^2}^{\sin(3x)} \sqrt{1 + t^4}\,dt \]
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

أوجد derivative \(h'(x)\) for the accumulation function: \[ h(x) = \int_{x^2}^{\sin(3x)} \sqrt{1 + t^4}\,dt \]

solution.en: Apply the Leibniz Rule with the Chain Rule: \[ h'(x) = \sqrt{1 + (\sin(3x))^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[\sin(3x)] - \sqrt{1 + (x^2)^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[x^2] \] Differentiating the boundary functions: \[ \frac{d}{dx}[\sin(3x)] = 3\cos(3x), \quad \frac{d}{dx}[x^2] = 2x \] Combining terms yields: \[ h'(x) = \mathbf{3\cos(3x)\sqrt{1 + \sin^4(3x)} - 2x\sqrt{1 + x^8}}. \]
solution.ar: Apply the Leibniz Rule with the Chain Rule: \[ h'(x) = \sqrt{1 + (\sin(3x))^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[\sin(3x)] - \sqrt{1 + (x^2)^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[x^2] \] Dإذا كانferentiating the boundary functions: \[ \frac{d}{dx}[\sin(3x)] = 3\cos(3x), \quad \frac{d}{dx}[x^2] = 2x \] Combining terms yields: \[ h'(x) = \mathbf{3\cos(3x)\sqrt{1 + \sin^4(3x)} - 2x\sqrt{1 + x^8}}. \]

hints.en: Apply the Leibniz Rule with the Chain Rule: \(h'(x) = \sqrt{1 + (\sin(3x))^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[\sin(3x)] - \sqrt{1 + (x^2)^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[x^2]\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(h'(x) = \sqrt{1 + (\sin(3x))^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[\sin(3x)] - \sqrt{1 + (x^2)^4} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[x^2]\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(h'(x)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Advanced u-Substitution & Inverse Trigonometric Forms

body.en: Substitution simplifies composite integrands by changing variables and transforming integration limits. Completing the square reveals standard inverse trigonometric forms.
body.ar: Substitution simplifies composite integrands by changing المتغيرات and transforming integration النهايات. Completing the square reveals standard inverse trigonometric forms.

label.en: ● Change of Variables & Inverse Trigonometric Antiderivative Library
label.ar: ● Change of المتغيرات & Inverse Trigonometric Antiderivative Library

body.en:
1. Definite Integration by Substitution: If \(g'\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(f\) is continuous on the range of \(u = g(x)\): \[ \int_a^b f(g(x))g'(x)\,dx = \int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)\,du \] Crucial AP Rule: Always convert the integration limits from \(x\) to \(u\). Writing \(\int_a^b f(u)\,du\) with mismatched variables and limits incurs an automatic deduction.

2. Core Inverse Trigonometric Antiderivatives (for \(a > 0\)): \[ \int \frac{du}{\sqrt{a^2 - u^2}} = \arcsin\left(\frac{u}{a}\right) + C \] \[ \int \frac{du}{a^2 + u^2} = \frac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\frac{u}{a}\right) + C \] \[ \int \frac{du}{|u|\sqrt{u^2 - a^2}} = \frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arcsec}\left(\frac{|u|}{a}\right) + C \]
body.ar:
1. Definite Integration by Substitution: If \(g'\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(f\) is continuous on the المدى of \(u = g(x)\): \[ \int_a^b f(g(x))g'(x)\,dx = \int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)\,du \] Crucial AP Rule: Always convert the integration النهايات from \(x\) to \(u\). Writing \(\int_a^b f(u)\,du\) with mismatched المتغيرات and النهايات incurs an automatic deduction.

2. Core Inverse Trigonometric Antiderivatives (for \(a > 0\)): \[ \int \frac{du}{\sqrt{a^2 - u^2}} = \arcsin\left(\frac{u}{a}\right) + C \] \[ \int \frac{du}{a^2 + u^2} = \frac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\frac{u}{a}\right) + C \] \[ \int \frac{du}{|u|\sqrt{u^2 - a^2}} = \frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arcsec}\left(\frac{|u|}{a}\right) + C \]

label.en: Level 3 (Advanced / FRQ) — Worked Example · Completing the Square & Trig Substitution
label.ar: Level 3 (Advanced / FRQ) — مثال محلول · Completing the Square & Trig Substitution

body.en:
Problem: Evaluate the definite integral: \[ \int_1^3 \frac{2x - 3}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx \]

Solution:

  1. Decompose the numerator into derivative of denominator plus constant: The derivative of \(x^2 - 2x + 5\) is \(2x - 2\). Rewrite: \[ 2x - 3 = (2x - 2) - 1 \] Split the integral into two terms: \[ \int_1^3 \frac{2x - 2}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx - \int_1^3 \frac{1}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx = I_1 - I_2 \]
  2. Evaluate \(I_1\) via logarithmic substitution: Let \(u = x^2 - 2x + 5 \implies du = (2x - 2)\,dx\).
    When \(x = 1\): \(u = 1 - 2 + 5 = 4\). When \(x = 3\): \(u = 9 - 6 + 5 = 8\). \[ I_1 = \int_4^8 \frac{1}{u}\,du = [\ln|u|]_4^8 = \ln 8 - \ln 4 = \ln\left(\frac{8}{4}\right) = \ln 2 \]
  3. Evaluate \(I_2\) by completing the square: \[ x^2 - 2x + 5 = (x - 1)^2 + 4 = (x - 1)^2 + 2^2 \] Let \(w = x - 1 \implies dw = dx\). Limits: \(x = 1 \implies w = 0\); \(x = 3 \implies w = 2\). \[ I_2 = \int_0^2 \frac{dw}{w^2 + 2^2} = \left[ \frac{1}{2}\arctan\left(\frac{w}{2}\right) \right]_0^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left( \arctan(1) - \arctan(0) \right) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - 0\right) = \frac{\pi}{8} \]
  4. Combine results: \[ \int_1^3 \frac{2x - 3}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx = \mathbf{\ln 2 - \frac{\pi}{8}} \approx 0.6931 - 0.3927 = 0.3004. \]
body.ar:
Problem: احسب قيمة definite التكامل: \[ \int_1^3 \frac{2x - 3}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx \]

Solution:

  1. Decompose the numerator into المشتقة of denominator plus الثابت: The المشتقة of \(x^2 - 2x + 5\) is \(2x - 2\). Rewrite: \[ 2x - 3 = (2x - 2) - 1 \] Split the التكامل into two terms: \[ \int_1^3 \frac{2x - 2}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx - \int_1^3 \frac{1}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx = I_1 - I_2 \]
  2. Evaluate \(I_1\) via logarithmic substitution: Let \(u = x^2 - 2x + 5 \implies du = (2x - 2)\,dx\).
    When \(x = 1\): \(u = 1 - 2 + 5 = 4\). عندما \(x = 3\): \(u = 9 - 6 + 5 = 8\). \[ I_1 = \int_4^8 \frac{1}{u}\,du = [\ln|u|]_4^8 = \ln 8 - \ln 4 = \ln\left(\frac{8}{4}\right) = \ln 2 \]
  3. Evaluate \(I_2\) by completing the square: \[ x^2 - 2x + 5 = (x - 1)^2 + 4 = (x - 1)^2 + 2^2 \] Let \(w = x - 1 \implies dw = dx\). النهايات: \(x = 1 \implies w = 0\); \(x = 3 \implies w = 2\). \[ I_2 = \int_0^2 \frac{dw}{w^2 + 2^2} = \left[ \frac{1}{2}\arctan\left(\frac{w}{2}\right) \right]_0^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left( \arctan(1) - \arctan(0) \right) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - 0\right) = \frac{\pi}{8} \]
  4. Combine results: \[ \int_1^3 \frac{2x - 3}{x^2 - 2x + 5}\,dx = \mathbf{\ln 2 - \frac{\pi}{8}} \approx 0.6931 - 0.3927 = 0.3004. \]

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Evaluate the definite integral using a substitution that transforms the limits: \[ \int_0^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} x \cos(x^2) e^{\sin(x^2)}\,dx \]
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

احسب قيمة the definite integral using a substitution that transforms the limits: \[ \int_0^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} x \cos(x^2) e^{\sin(x^2)}\,dx \]

solution.en:
Let \(u = \sin(x^2)\). Differentiating gives \(du = \cos(x^2) \cdot 2x\,dx = 2x\cos(x^2)\,dx \implies x\cos(x^2)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}du\).
Transform the integration limits:

  • Lower limit \(x = 0 \implies u = \sin(0) = 0\).
  • Upper limit \(x = \sqrt{\pi/2} \implies u = \sin((\sqrt{\pi/2})^2) = \sin(\pi/2) = 1\).
Substitute into the integral: \[ \int_0^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} x\cos(x^2) e^{\sin(x^2)}\,dx = \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 e^u\,du = \frac{1}{2} \left[ e^u \right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{2}(e^1 - e^0) = \mathbf{\frac{e - 1}{2}} \approx 0.8591. \]
solution.ar:
ليكن \(u = \sin(x^2)\). Dإذا كانferentiating gives \(du = \cos(x^2) \cdot 2x\,dx = 2x\cos(x^2)\,dx \implies x\cos(x^2)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}du\).
Transform the integration limits:

  • Lower limit \(x = 0 \implies u = \sin(0) = 0\).
  • Upper limit \(x = \sqrt{\pi/2} \implies u = \sin((\sqrt{\pi/2})^2) = \sin(\pi/2) = 1\).
عوّض into the integral: \[ \int_0^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} x\cos(x^2) e^{\sin(x^2)}\,dx = \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 e^u\,du = \frac{1}{2} \left[ e^u \right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{2}(e^1 - e^0) = \mathbf{\frac{e - 1}{2}} \approx 0.8591. \]

hints.en: Transform the integration limits: Lower limit \(x = 0 \implies u = \sin(0) = 0\). Upper limit \(x = \sqrt{\pi/2} \implies u = \sin((\sqrt{\pi/2})^2) = \sin(\pi/2)\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(x = 0 \implies u = \sin(0) = 0\) ، \(x = \sqrt{\pi/2} \implies u = \sin((\sqrt{\pi/2})^2) = \sin(\pi/2)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Substitute into the integral: \(\int_0^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} x\cos(x^2) e^{\sin(x^2)}\,dx = \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 e^u\,du = \frac{1}{2} \left[ e^u \right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{2}(e^1 - e^0) = \mathbf{\frac{e - 1}{2}}\).
hints.ar: عوّض into the integral: \(\int_0^{\sqrt{\pi/2}} x\cos(x^2) e^{\sin(x^2)}\,dx = \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 e^u\,du = \frac{1}{2} \left[ e^u \right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{2}(e^1 - e^0) = \mathbf{\frac{e - 1}{2}}\).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the derivative of a function \( f(x) \), denoted by \( f'(x) \), is shown in the figure above. The function \( f(x) \) is continuous, and it is known that \( f(1) = 5 \). Determine the value of \( f(5) \).
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Medium] The graph of the derivative of a function \( f(x) \), denoted by \( f'(x) \), is shown in the figure above. The function \( f(x) \) is continuous, and it is known that \( f(1) = 5 \). حدّد value of \( f(5) \).

hints.en: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus states that \( \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx = f(b) - f(a) \). Rearranging this, we get \( f(b) = f(a) + \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx = f(b) - f(a) \) ، \( f(b) = f(a) + \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: This is a triangle with base \( 3 - 1 = 2 \) and height \( f'(1) = 3 \). The area of this triangle is \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( 3 - 1 = 2 \) ، \( f'(1) = 3 \) ، \(\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus states that \( \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx = f(b) - f(a) \). Rearranging this, we get \( f(b) = f(a) + \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx \).

In this problem, we are given \( f(1) = 5 \) and we need to find \( f(5) \). Thus, we have \( a = 1 \) and \( b = 5 \). We need to calculate the definite integral \( \int_{1}^{5} f'(x) \, dx \), which represents the area under the curve of \( f'(x) \) from \( x=1 \) to \( x=5 \).

From the graph, \( f'(x) \) is a straight line. The area from \( x=1 \) to \( x=5 \) can be split into two parts: a triangle and a rectangle.

Part 1: Area from \( x=1 \) to \( x=3 \).
This is a triangle with base \( 3 - 1 = 2 \) and height \( f'(1) = 3 \). The area of this triangle is \( \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3 = 3 \).

Part 2: Area from \( x=3 \) to \( x=5 \).
This is a rectangle with base \( 5 - 3 = 2 \) and height \( f'(3) = 3 \). The area of this rectangle is \( \text{base} \times \text{height} = 2 \times 3 = 6 \).

Therefore, the total area under the curve from \( x=1 \) to \( x=5 \) is \( \int_{1}^{5} f'(x) \, dx = 3 + 6 = 9 \).

Now, we can find \( f(5) \): \( f(5) = f(1) + \int_{1}^{5} f'(x) \, dx = 5 + 9 = 14 \).

Common traps: Students might misinterpret the graph and assume \( f'(x) \) is constant or linear over the entire interval without splitting it. They might also make calculation errors with the area of the triangle or rectangle.
solution.ar:
The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus states that \( \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx = f(b) - f(a) \). Rearranging this, we get \( f(b) = f(a) + \int_{a}^{b} f'(x) \, dx \).

In this problem, we are given \( f(1) = 5 \) and we need to أوجد \( f(5) \). وعليه، we have \( a = 1 \) and \( b = 5 \). We need to احسب definite integral \( \int_{1}^{5} f'(x) \, dx \), which represents the area under the curve of \( f'(x) \) from \( x=1 \) to \( x=5 \).

From the graph, \( f'(x) \) is a straight line. The area from \( x=1 \) to \( x=5 \) can be split into two parts: a triangle and a rectangle.

Part 1: Area from \( x=1 \) to \( x=3 \).
This is a triangle with base \( 3 - 1 = 2 \) and height \( f'(1) = 3 \). The area of this triangle is \( \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3 = 3 \).

Part 2: Area from \( x=3 \) to \( x=5 \).
This is a rectangle with base \( 5 - 3 = 2 \) and height \( f'(3) = 3 \). The area of this rectangle is \( \text{base} \times \text{height} = 2 \times 3 = 6 \).

وبالتالي، the total area under the curve from \( x=1 \) to \( x=5 \) is \( \int_{1}^{5} f'(x) \, dx = 3 + 6 = 9 \).

Now, we can أوجد \( f(5) \): \( f(5) = f(1) + \int_{1}^{5} f'(x) \, dx = 5 + 9 = 14 \).

Common traps: Students might misinterpret the graph and assume \( f'(x) \) is constant or linear over the entire interval without splitting it. They might also make calculation errors with the area of the triangle or rectangle.

question.en: Consider the function \( f(x) = 4 \). What is the value of the definite integral \( \int_{3}^{6} f(x) \, dx \)?
question.ar: Consider the function \( f(x) = 4 \). ما قيمة the definite integral \( \int_{3}^{6} f(x) \, dx \)?

hints.en: The definite integral \( \int_{a}^{b} c \, dx \) where c is a constant represents the area of a rectangle with height c and width \( b-a \).
hints.ar: The definite integral \( \int_{a}^{b} c \, dx \) حيث c is a constant represents the area of a rectangle with height c and width \( b-a \).

hints.en: In this case, \( c = 4 \), \( a = 3 \), and \( b = 6 \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( c = 4 \) ، \( a = 3 \) ، \( b = 6 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Therefore, the value of the integral is \(4 \times (6-3) = 4 \times 3\).
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the value of the integral is \(4 \times (6-3) = 4 \times 3\).

solution.en: The definite integral \( \int_{a}^{b} c \, dx \) where c is a constant represents the area of a rectangle with height c and width \( b-a \). In this case, \( c = 4 \), \( a = 3 \), and \( b = 6 \). Therefore, the value of the integral is \( 4 \times (6-3) = 4 \times 3 = 12 \).
